trust_decision.summary: Whether a log field may carry a line separator is decided by escapeLogField's character class (index.js:60-76), and it is invoked at exactly one place: the built-in :remote-user token (index.js:351). Every other token's value travels from its own function (e.g. :referrer index.js:331-333, :user-agent index.js:375-377, :req index.js:383-390) through compile()'s string concatenation (index.js:453) or a user format function (index.js:150) into stream.write(line + '\n') (index.js:161) unchecked, so U+0085/U+2028/U+2029 in a header or in a Basic-auth username still forges log lines.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'unescaped Unicode line separators'; the only escaping code in the tree is the escapeLogField regex, so an engineer widens /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f\\]/ to add \u0085, \u2028 and \u2029 — which changes behaviour for :remote-user only, because index.js:351 is escapeLogField's sole caller.

fix_sites.entry_point: morgan(format) with any string/named format (compile at index.js:439-458) and every token value routed through escapeLogField
morgan(':remote-user') / the built-in :remote-user token, i.e. the default, combined, common and short formats (index.js:184-196)
morgan.token(name, fn) — the public registration API; the fix wraps fn so its string value is escaped wherever it is read

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Escaping is the token's job, not the line's: README.md:200-202 says a token callback is 'expected to return a string value', and HISTORY.md:5-7 scopes the earlier log-injection fix to 'the `:remote-user` token' — so a format function's own return value, a format function used as a token, or a token returning a non-string can each be argued to be the application author's responsibility.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Object-mode pass-through: with stream.writableObjectMode and a format function returning an object, the object must reach the stream as-is with no trailing newline (README.md:111-114, test/morgan.js:1222-1245). An over-broad fix that escapes or stringifies the assembled line in logRequest breaks it; the same over-broad move also escapes the dev format's own ANSI codes (index.js:233-234, test/morgan.js:1387-1529, and the 102/500 cases).

O6_input_shapes: array-valued header joined with ', ' before escaping — :req[set-cookie] and :res (index.js:387-389, index.js:404-406)
Basic-auth username decoded from Base64, carrying C1 U+0085 and U+2028/U+2029 (index.js:345-353)
token values read from a user format function (tokens.req(req, res, field)) instead of a compiled format string (fix.diff:51-73)
non-string token returns — numeric :status, millisecond strings, undefined — which the fix's typeof guard leaves untouched (fix.diff:37-40)
object returns for object-mode streams, which likewise must pass through untouched

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A format function returns a request/response-derived string directly (morgan(function (tokens, req, res) { return req.headers['x-test'] })) — formatLine's output goes to the sink unescaped; the fix only escapes values that came out of a token.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A format function's return value is the application's own line, not a morgan token; escaping it would double-escape token values and destroy object-mode output, so it is the caller's job.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 11 lines above the sink and ~90 lines below the landing point; no package boundary

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A custom token returns a non-string (morgan.token('cookies', function (req) { return req.headers['set-cookie'] })): the wrapper's typeof string guard skips it and compile()'s concatenation at index.js:453 coerces the array into the line, so separators inside an element survive even after the published fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: README.md:200-202 documents the contract as 'expected to return a string value', so a non-string return is the token author's bug, not a morgan flaw.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; the gap sits between the fix's wrapper (index.js:587-590) and compile()'s coercion (index.js:453)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A function registered with morgan.format(name, fn) and then referenced as :name in a format string resolves through the shared namespace (compile looks up tokens['name'] on the morgan object, index.js:447) to the raw unwrapped function, so its return value is concatenated unescaped.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Formats and tokens are separate documented features (README.md:293-307); using a named format as a token is undocumented, so the route is unsupported rather than uncovered.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; the registration site (index.js:500-503) is ~85 lines from the token() wrapper the fix changes

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second built-in header token (cookies, session id, x-forwarded-for list) that joins a multi-valued header itself before returning it.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: README.md:207 already advertises reading a raw header in a custom token, and the :req/:res tokens show the project is happy to own the array-to-string join — a maintainer would plausibly add such a token next to these.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Buffered writes: createBufferStream batches already-formatted lines before the single user-stream write.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the only other code that writes to the user stream (the deprecated `buffer` option, index.js:119-129); an escaping fix placed at the stream.write call sites could easily cover one and not the other.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Per-status compiled format functions cached in developmentFormatLine, capturing a token value at compile time.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The dev format already caches compiled sub-formats per colour; a maintainer extending dev output could capture a token value there, producing a path where the check never re-invokes the token.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The deprecated object form morgan({ format: ... }) that merges options and picks the format.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is a live defaults/merge route kept for back-compatibility (deprecate() call at index.js:96), exactly the sort of legacy path a fix bypasses.

O9_family: log injection / improper neutralization of output for logs (CWE-117) — line-separator forging in log fields

O10_build.toolchain: npm; mocha 10.8.2, supertest 4.0.2, split 1.0.1, eslint 6.8.0, nyc 15.1.0 (package.json:28-40); no node_modules vendored, so one npm install is required
O10_build.project_tests: test/morgan.js (~1.6k lines of mocha + supertest against in-process http/https servers, TLS cert fixtures in test/fixtures) and test/noColor.js; npm test runs both with --check-leaks (package.json:51). Escaping coverage exists only under :remote-user (test/morgan.js:559-679).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Extend the escapeLogField character class to cover \u0085/\u2028/\u2029 and stop there — its only caller is :remote-user, so the default format's :referrer and :user-agent, :req[...], :url and every function-format token stay forgeable.
